record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Dynamics of Quadratic and Higher Degree Polynomial ODE Systems
record.original_question: For the quadratic systems x' = y^2 - z + A, y' = z, z' = x and x' = y, y' = -x + yz, z' = 1 - y^2, prove that the numerically observed intersections of certain trajectories with their indicated Poincaré sections have fractal dimension, and then determine whether the corresponding systems are chaotic. Concretely, show that for the first system at least one trajectory intersects the section x = 0 in a set with nontrivial thickness, and that for the second system at least one trajectory intersects the section z = 0 in a set with nontrivial thickness; then decide whether those observations imply genuine chaos.

evidence.quote: 3.5. Fifth Open Problem From Fig. 3.2, and Fig. 3.3 it appears that system (3.24) has at least one solution such that it intersects the Poincaré section x = 0 into a set with “thickness”. Similarly from Fig. 3.4, it appears that system (3.25) has at least one solution that intersects the Poincaré section z = 0 into a set also with “thickness”. This open problem is to show that these sets have fractal dimensions. A further question is to show that this system is chaotic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two autonomous three-dimensional quadratic ODE systems

(I)  x' = y² − z + A,   y' = z,   z' = x,

where A ∈ ℝ is a real parameter, and

(II) x' = y,   y' = −x + y z,   z' = 1 − y².

Numerical experiments suggest that system (I) admits at least one bounded trajectory whose successive intersections with the Poincaré section {x = 0} accumulate on a set of nonzero "thickness" (i.e. not contained in a smooth one-dimensional curve), and likewise that system (II) admits at least one bounded trajectory whose successive intersections with the Poincaré section {z = 0} accumulate on a set of nonzero "thickness".

(a) Prove rigorously that for some choice of parameter A and some initial condition, the corresponding Poincaré return set of system (I) on {x = 0} has non-integer Hausdorff (or box-counting) dimension strictly between 1 and 2.

(b) Prove the analogous statement for system (II): there exists an initial condition whose Poincaré return set on {z = 0} has fractal (non-integer) dimension strictly between 1 and 2.

(c) Determine, with proof, whether either of these systems is genuinely chaotic in the sense of possessing a positive topological entropy or a positive Lyapunov exponent on an invariant set, and in particular whether the observed "thickness" of the Poincaré sections implies genuine chaotic dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: No published rigorous proof was located establishing the fractal dimension of the Poincaré return sets for these specific minimal quadratic three-dimensional ODE systems, nor a rigorous proof of chaos for them. The problem appears in collected open-problem lists on the dynamics of low-term quadratic ODEs (associated with the Heidel–Zhang program on minimal chaotic quadratic systems) and remains unresolved in the literature accessible online.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in chaos theory and dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems on minimal quadratic 3D ODE systems, including questions about fractal Poincaré sections and chaos.
status_evidence.claim: The fractal-dimension and chaos questions for these minimal quadratic systems are listed as open problems.

status_evidence.title: Chaos theory - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General background on strange attractors, Poincaré sections, and fractal dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: No specific resolution for the systems in question is reported in the standard literature.
